text: I'll start with the paged deployment and its pod.

remediation.name: checkout-worker
remediation.required_value: env entry name: AMQP_URL with the queue connection string, e.g. value: amqp://user:pass@rabbitmq.payments.svc.cluster.local:5672/ (or valueFrom a ConfigMap/Secret key that exists in namespace payments)

arguments.root_cause_statement: The checkout-worker Deployment's pod template declares no environment variables, but its container command requires AMQP_URL and exits immediately when that variable is empty. Each container start prints "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set" and terminates with exit code 1, so the kubelet backs the container off into CrashLoopBackOff and the pod never becomes Ready, leaving the Deployment at 0/1 Ready and no consumer draining the checkout queue. Nothing in the namespace supplies the value either: the only ConfigMap present is kube-root-ca.crt and the pod template contains no configMapKeyRef, secretKeyRef or envFrom. The fix is to add an AMQP_URL env entry to the worker container in the Deployment pod template.
arguments.mechanism: Deployment payments/checkout-worker has no .spec.template.spec.containers[worker].env, so AMQP_URL is unset in the container; its command guard `[ -n "${AMQP_URL:-}" ] || { echo "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set"; exit 1; }` fires and the worker exits with code 1 on every start, driving CrashLoopBackOff and keeping the Deployment at 0/1 Ready. It needs an env entry named AMQP_URL carrying the queue connection string instead of no env at all.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment is 0/1 Ready and its only pod is in CrashLoopBackOff after 5 restarts with lastExit=Error.
The Deployment pod template defines a container command that exits 1 unless AMQP_URL is set, and defines no env at all.
The previous container instance died printing exactly that fatal message, proving AMQP_URL was empty at runtime.
The running pod has no environment variables injected and terminated with exit code 1, then went to CrashLoopBackOff.
The kubelet is restarting the failed worker container in a back-off loop, which is what holds the Deployment at 0/1 Ready.
evidence.quote: Back-off restarting failed container worker in pod checkout-worker-66bfcdfc47-d9gdj_payments

ruled_out.alternative: A ConfigMap key reference that no longer resolves (missing or renamed key) is the source of the empty AMQP_URL.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The namespace holds only the auto-injected kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap, and the pod template contains no configMapKeyRef/envFrom at all, so nothing was ever wired up to fail to resolve.

ruled_out.alternative: Image pull failure or scheduling/capacity problem prevents the worker from running.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod was scheduled and the image was already present and started six times; the container starts fine and then exits on its own.
ruled_out.quote: Container image "busybox:1.36" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod

ruled_out.alternative: A Service selector or endpoints mismatch is why checkout jobs are not consumed.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The namespace contains no Services at all — only the Deployment, its pod, one ConfigMap and one ServiceAccount — so no selector could be involved.
